articles.title_orig: 5 takeaways from Kemi Badenoch’s fighty Tory conference speech
articles.title_zh: 5 takeaways from Kemi Badenoch’s fighty Tory conference speech
articles.content_orig:
BIRMINGHAM, England — Kemi Badenoch used her rare moment in the spotlight Wednesday to promise “a fight coming in British politics; a fight that we have not seen in this country for more than half a century.”
Britain’s opposition Conservative leader, speaking at the close of her party’s annual conference in Birmingham, started as she meant to go on. She attacked Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s Labour Party and her right-wing rivals, Nigel Farage’s Reform UK.
It was a speech more about positioning the Tories in a five-party system than about policy. What little she did announce was also about positioning.
Badenoch’s flagship pledge was to abolish inheritance tax on a person’s main home, which is currently set at a threshold of £500,000 (or £1 million for a married couple). It will overwhelmingly benefit the wealthiest families — but it’s part of Badenoch’s argument about being unashamedly Tory and pursuing growth.
On her own terms, and those of her members, Badenoch is seeing the conference as a success. This time last year her own party was muttering about her future; now it is united in pursuing a victory at the next general election.
Whether she can achieve that victory is another question. POLITICO’s Poll of Polls puts the Conservative Party on just 18% in a general election (due by 2029), beneath its historic low in 2024, and behind Reform on 22% and Labour on 26%.
POLITICO crunched the five biggest takeaways as Tory conference closed.
With most polls projecting a hung parliament, the shape of Britain’s next government could be decided by one thing: whether the Tories are willing — or able — to form a pact with the rival right-wing party Reform UK.
Badenoch’s speech suggests that they are neither — and made it personal. Badenoch, the first Black leader of a major U.K. political party, took aim at Reform politicians and outriders who have questioned if non-white Brits with foreign heritage can be classed as English.
“I don’t want to explain to my son when we’re watching our brilliant England team play football that some people don’t think our black players are English,” she said. “We must not let these people take us backwards. That is not the country we are … I am black. I am British. I am proud of my country.”
She added: “To those who say unite the right: We are not uniting with that.”
At the same time, her party is clearly turning its head to middle-class “shire Tories” in the south of England who switched to the Liberal Democrats in 2024. Some of the key policies announced this week — such as state-subsidized childcare for workers earning more than £100,000 a year, and scrapping inheritance tax on multi-million-pound family homes — will benefit wealthier voters in London and the south.
That is a very different voter coalition to the industrial heartlands in northern England, where low-income voters have turned to Reform. “None of our voters would benefit from this tax cut for the 2%,” boasted one Reform aide of the Tory inheritance tax policy. “They’ve abandoned going after our voters.” (Tory aides insist they have policies to win back both groups.)
So could Badenoch’s Conservatives form a pact with any other party? The jury’s out on that.
She spent little energy criticizing the hard-right Restore Britain – which could aid her party by splitting Reform’s vote – but Restore’s tally of seats at an election would be minimal.
And while the Tories governed with the centrist Liberal Democrats in 2010, both sides remain scarred from that. Meanwhile, Burnham has already laid out what sounded like a coalition pitch last week, when he argued for closer ties with the EU and electoral reform. Shadow Minister for Policy Renewal Neil O’Brien told a fringe event: “Not since Marilyn Monroe stood on that hot air vent and let her skirts billow have I seen such a ‘come hither’ gesture.”
Badenoch’s speech focused overwhelmingly on attacking her rivals and creating clear space between her party and theirs.
Burnham was the “Paddington Bear prime minister who hopes our problems go away”; Tory defector Robert Jenrick was part of an “export boom of drama queens going to Reform”; the Green Party was guilty of “disgraceful antisemitism”; some Reform politicians are “measuring up the curtains for their prison cells.” Her autocue even instructed her to give “side eye” when mocking Farage’s ally George Cottrell, whose links to the Reform leader have come under scrutiny.
It was a deliberate contrast to Burnham’s speech last week, which avoided naming his rivals. In a five- or six-party market, the two leaders are taking opposite approaches to make themselves stand out: Burnham wants to rise above the melee while Badenoch thew the hardest punches.
They are united, though, in seeing politics as a battle of ideas — unlike former PM Keir Starmer, accused of focusing more on process than vision. Badenoch spent more than two months personally writing a 95-page treatise on her ideas about the future, “The Right Way.” She unveiled it on the conference’s first day; extraordinarily, it didn’t leak.
Badenoch also wants to cut through by presenting her party as the voice of fiscal responsibility and defense. The Tories announced what they said would amount to £13 billion a year in welfare cuts on top of £23 billion announced last year. “Our country is running out of money. Almost every other problem flows from this,” said Badenoch.
She added her party would end the “delays” and approve a third runway for Heathrow Airport (though the exact process for this was not clear), halve the 15 percent rate of employers’ national insurance for under-25s and overturn the Labour government’s reforms to employment rights.
The Conservatives are banking on Burnham’s star falling after the Oct. 28 budget and a difficult spending review next year, in which he will have to set out whether Britain spends 3% of its GDP on defense by 2030.
A shadow cabinet minister, granted anonymity to speak frankly, said: “It’s a make-do-and-mend budget; they’ll get through that — but they can’t get through the spending review. [Former Chancellor] Rachel [Reeves] left them a bomb primed to explode.”
The ideological chasm being opened up between Badenoch and Burnham is forcing the Conservatives onto uncomfortable territory.
Burnham used his own conference speech to open the door to a possible return to the EU, but Badenoch was clear she didn’t want to take the bait.
“He [Burnham] wants to reopen the Brexit debate. Can you imagine having to go through that again?” the Tory leader said. “So much time lost arguing with ourselves, arguing with the EU, going round and round in circles, businesses not knowing whether they should invest. He wants to do it all again. I think that is a terrible idea.”
Public opinion has shifted in the decade since the EU referendum, which was triggered and implemented by the Conservatives. Renegotiating any new deal with Brussels will be a headache for Burnham and stacked with peril, but it’ll also serve as a reminder of what the Tories — and veteran Brexit campaigner Farage — delivered for the country.
Veteran Euroskeptic MP Bernard Jenkin was even blunter at a fringe event: “Do not defend Brexit. Brexit is toxic with the voters.”
The other big divide that Burnham opened up is on social care. He wants to fund a “national care service” for the elderly in part by changing the “triple lock” on state pensions.
That lock is cherished by many on the right — but there are also the small-state realists who want it axed to curtail the ballooning welfare bill. POLITICO reported that shadow cabinet ministers are debating not coming up with their own substantive offer on how to fix the care system.
“The Tories are ducking the big issues facing our country and instead of showing leadership, Kemi Badenoch is happy to fail a whole generation of older people who have contributed to society all their lives,” Labour Party chair Bridget Phillipson responded.

articles.title_orig: Nobel chemistry prize goes to pair who solved mystery of 'mirror image' molecules
articles.title_zh: Nobel chemistry prize goes to pair who solved mystery of 'mirror image' molecules
articles.content_orig:
The Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to French scientist Henri B. Kagan and Japan's Kenso Soai for providing a solution to the chemical mystery of life's asymmetry.
The researchers discovered how nature exclusively makes the correct version of a molecule - rather than its mirror image.
For example, amino acid molecules, the building blocks of proteins, exist as two forms that are each other's mirror image.
But living organisms on Earth only function with one of those forms. The Nobel laureates answered the question: why does life favour just one of these mirror image molecules over the other.
In organic chemistry, this property is known as "chirality", so chiral molecules have both right and left-handed forms.
You can think of them as looking like our hands - not identical, but each a mirror image of the other.
And while nature almost exclusively produces the version it requires to function, chemical reactions in a lab usually create a 50-50 mix of both left- and right-handed molecules.
When it comes to making drugs, this is particularly significant, because each version behaves differently when it interacts with our bodies.
So, one might have disease-fighting properties, while the other version does nothing or even causes harm.
The development of the Thalidomide drug is an example of this. In the 1950s it was prescribed to pregnant women suffering with morning sickness. But it is a chiral molecule - the right-handed version is an effective treatment, but the left-hand is toxic.
The original drug given was a mixture of the two, and it was later discovered that the body will convert between the two. The result was thousands of children, born to women who took the drug, developed severe disabilities.
Speaking to the Nobel Prize press conference this morning over the phone, Kenso Soai said: "This is one of the most exciting days of my life."
By solving the mystery of chirality, Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai worked out how to design chemical reactions to produce much more of the desired version of a molecule.
Heiner Linke, chair of the Nobel Committee for Chemistry, explained: "Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai have provided a solution to a chemical mystery that is over a century old: how homochirality - the selective production of the correct version of a molecule - can emerge spontaneously.
"The chemical reactions they have developed are spectacular."
Henri Kagan, who is at Université Paris-Sud, first discovered a new way of manipulating chemical reactions in 1986. This allowed him to create a greater excess of one of the mirror images than had previously been thought possible.
Kenso Soai from Tokyo University of Science took the next step in 1995. He published a scientific paper in the journal Nature describing the first ever chemical reaction that had the potential to be homochiral - producing only the desired version of an organic molecule.
In 2003, he finally succeeded in controlling a reaction in which only one of the two possible mirror images was formed.
"Other than life itself," the Nobel Committee said in a statement, "no one had previously achieved this feat".
At the press conference on Wednesday, Kenso Soai praised the "many, many excellent researchers" in this field.
Professor Robert Mokaya, president of the UK's Royal Society of Chemistry said it was a "powerful example of how fundamental chemistry can underpin solutions to some of the biggest challenges facing society".
"Different isomers (or versions of molecules) can have completely different biological and physical effects, so they are crucial in finding effective medicines to treat all sorts of illnesses," he added.
Prof Angus Davison, from the University of Nottingham, studies the biology of chirality and said that the Nobel-winning chemistry could help reveal how and why life favours "one-handedness".
"In ways that we don't yet quite understand, the chirality of the basic building blocks of life ends up making bodies that are themselves also chiral," he told BBC News.
This was the foundation, he explained, of our hearts being on left hand side of our bodies and snail shells that coil to the right.
Peter Somfai, a member of the Nobel Committee for Chemistry, said the research awarded this year's prize has become part of "our basic understanding of how chemistry functions".
He said showing how a mirror image is created is "probably the most fundamental question in life - because somehow that happened four billion years ago when life was created. And now we have, for the first time, mimicked that in the lab".

articles.title_orig: Exclusive | France Considers Issuing More Shorter-Term Debt After Bond-Market Turmoil
articles.title_zh: Exclusive | France Considers Issuing More Shorter-Term Debt After Bond-Market Turmoil
articles.content_orig:
France’s unprecedented wave of student protests has laid bare the country’s growing financial pressures, which will only become more difficult to tackle as Europe’s second-largest economy tries to rein in a ballooning budget deficit.
The country’s finances are in a precarious state. Public debt was more than $4 trillion in June, exceeding the size of the economy, according to the country’s statistics agency . The cost of servicing that debt has climbed by billions of dollars on last year, as bond yields spike .
At the same time, demands on the public purse are rising: Pension costs have climbed because of an aging population while the government looks to spend more on defense.
High school students, meanwhile, have called for a fix to staff shortages, overcrowded classrooms and crumbling school infrastructure.
Solutions to France’s financial troubles have led to social unrest in the past. Efforts to raise the retirement age sparked widespread protests in 2023 .
French school protests grow as workers join students
Last week, the French government proposed deep spending cuts and tax hikes aimed at narrowing the budget deficit, but bond buyers are concerned that fiscal measures may be watered down by lawmakers ahead of presidential elections next year, said Andrew Kenningham, chief European economist at consultancy Capital Economics.
The election could see President Emmanuel Macron ousted by either a far-right or far-left successor, raising questions over the country’s commitment to fiscal discipline. While Marine Le Pen’s right-wing National Rally recently proposed substantial spending cuts meant to stabilize the public finances, her party also remains committed to costly tax reductions, Kenningham said.
“Investors will also be concerned about greater fiscal populism after the elections,” he wrote in a note last week. “There is a big risk that spreads rise a lot further, either before or after next year’s elections.”
Worries about a potential debt crisis in France boiled over last week, leading to a selloff in French bonds and a sharp rise in yields.
The spread between French and German bond yields expanded to its widest level since 2012. That difference in yields means investors are demanding much higher returns to hold debt from France compared with Germany, which is deemed a safer alternative.
The French bond rout has sparked fears of spillovers to other high-yield European debt markets, with some analysts drawing parallels with the eurozone debt crisis of the early 2010s .
Global bond sell-off deepens, sending borrowing costs higher around the world
Given France’s size and systemic importance, “the potential for contagion into other countries and the Eurozone at large is very large and could potentially cause a serious crisis for the entire region,” Angel Talavera, chief European economist at Oxford Economics, an advisory firm, told CNN.
These worries in large part pushed the euro to its weakest level against the dollar since May 2025 on Monday. The currency, shared by 21 countries in the European Union, is worth around $1.12, having briefly dipped below that level.
The latest ructions in markets could weigh on a fragile economic recovery in Europe, bolstered by investment into artificial intelligence, stronger demand for European exports and higher defense spending in Germany.
Recent survey data showed that activity in manufacturing and services in the euro area increased at its fastest pace in nearly three-and-a-half years last month.
“(Economic) growth is staging a comeback and Europe has shown surprising resilience,” economists at Morgan Stanley wrote in a late September note.
Fall of yet another premier will make it hard for France to fix its finances. What’s behind its debt problem?
High bond yields are a clear risk to that growth, however.
If governments don’t cut spending , “interest rates will continue to go up,” Carsten Brzeski, head of macroeconomics at Dutch bank ING told CNN.
Higher bond yields push up the cost of borrowing throughout the economy, making home and car purchases more expensive and driving down investment. They also make it more expensive for governments to borrow money and force a certain degree of austerity to stop yields from rising further.
Yields on French, German and UK government bonds have broken multi-year records in recent weeks as concerns mount about the sustainability of public debt loads.
Europe’s public finances pose “serious risks to eurozone financial markets and to the economy,” Jack Allen-Reynolds, deputy chief eurozone economist at Capital Economics, told CNN.

articles.title_orig: Tropical Storm Isaias forms in Gulf, could reach U.S. as hurricane this weekend. See maps, possible path.
articles.title_zh: Tropical Storm Isaias forms in Gulf, could reach U.S. as hurricane this weekend. See maps, possible path.
articles.content_orig:
Hurricane, tropical storm and storm surge watches have been issued for parts of the U.S. Gulf Coast as Tropical Storm Isaias was expected to approach that area Friday after becoming a hurricane, according to the National Hurricane Center .
Currently swirling in the Gulf, Isaias would be the Atlantic Basin's first hurricane of the season and is its ninth named storm. El Niño continues to bring a more active season in the Pacific. The storm formed with less than two months remaining in the 2026 hurricane season , which ends Nov. 30.
Tropical Storm Isaias, which grew from Tropical Depression Nine on Wednesday and is pronounced "ees-ah-EE-ahs," is expected to pass to the north of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula on Thursday before approaching the U.S. Gulf Coast the following day, according to forecasters. It is expected to rapidly strengthen.
A hurricane watch was issued Wednesday for the northern Gulf Coast, from Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, to Indian Pass, Florida, and a tropical storm watch was issued from Bay St. Louis to Louisiana's Jefferson/Plaquemines Parish line and from Indian Pass to Florida's Aucilla River. A storm surge watch was also effected from the mouth of the Mississippi River to Yankeetown, Florida, according to the hurricane center.
Tropical storm-force winds were extending outward up to 45 miles from the storm's center on Wednesday morning.
Isaias is forecast to bring moderate to heavy rainfall to the Gulf Coast and into the rest of the Southeast this weekend into early next week. The hurricane center forecasts 3 to 6 inches of rain and as much as 10 inches in some places on the central Gulf Coast from southeastern Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle.
Some longer-range forecast models also see this moisture eventually reaching the Ohio Valley and Northeast by midweek next week.
The hurricane center on Thursday warned of "an increasing risk of dangerous wind and storm surge impacts" along parts of the northern Gulf Coast and urged people living in Louisiana, Alabama, Mississippi and northern Florida to "closely monitor the latest forecast updates and ensure they have their hurricane plan in place."
In addition to rain, the hurricane center said Isaias could potentially bring urban flooding and isolated river flooding to places in its path.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis on Tuesday signed an executive order declaring a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties ahead of the storm's arrival. DeSantis said in a statement that the order "ensures communities have the time and resources necessary to prepare for potential severe weather impacts to the Panhandle and Big Bend region of Florida."
While tropical storm and hurricane formation and frequency vary throughout the season, the "I"-named systems tend to be the most retired names within the Atlantic basin.
The most commonly known retired "I"-named storms are Ian (2022), Ida (2021), Irma (2017), and Irene (2011).
When Ike was retired in 2008, Isaias replaced the "I" name on the Atlantic tropical cyclones list, which rotates every six years.

articles.title_orig: Indie Selects for October 2026: Discover and Progress Through Unforgettable Worlds
articles.title_zh: Indie Selects for October 2026: Discover and Progress Through Unforgettable Worlds
articles.content_orig:
Every Wednesday, dive into the Indie Select Hub — your gateway to a fresh, curated indie collection plus four themed spotlights that rotate weekly! You can always find this collection hub in the XBOX Store and on XBOX.com/IndieSelects.
Halloween has never been just about scares. Sure, there’s plenty of room for heart-pounding frights, but it’s also a season that celebrates imagination, creativity, and stepping into worlds beyond the ordinary. This month, indie developers embraced that spirit in unforgettable ways.
For October, the ID@XBOX team has curated six standout Indie Selects that invite you to discover mysterious realms, conquer new challenges, and uncover stories waiting to be told. From epic battles and eldritch horrors to cozy puzzles and island adventures, each game offers a richly crafted world filled with surprises around every corner.
So, whether you’re seeking thrills, mystery, or a new adventure to get lost in, here are this month’s Indie Selects (in no particular order):
Mortal Shell II is still unapologetically challenging, but combat feels faster and more aggressive this time around. The removal of the traditional stamina gauge means encounters aren’t simply about waiting for a bar to refill. You can stay in the fight, combining melee weapons, sidearms, abilities and brutal executions. It makes combat feel considerably more fluid than before.
The world has grown too. Rather than simply pushing you down a predetermined path, Mortal Shell II encourages exploration across a compact, interconnected open world filled with hidden areas, dungeons, weapons, upgrades and, naturally, plenty of horrible things waiting to ruin your afternoon.
What I particularly enjoy is that exploration feels connected to progression. Finding another Shell isn’t just another collectible checked off a list. It can completely change how you approach the game. Weapons offer extensive upgrade paths as well, giving you plenty of room to shape your own approach to combat.
Mortal Shell II certainly isn’t interested in making life easy for you, but there’s something satisfying about gradually turning the tables. You go from cautiously approaching every new enemy to becoming the nightmare wandering through their world.
If you enjoy dark fantasy, exploration, challenging combat and the satisfaction of mastering a game that initially seems determined to destroy you, Mortal Shell II is absolutely worth having on your radar.
If you’ve ever wondered what it would be like to assemble your dream team of benders and settle legendary rivalries yourself , Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game is ready to make that happen. This 2D tag-team fighter brings together iconic characters from “Avatar: The Last Airbender” and “The Legend of Korra,” combining elemental bending, flashy special moves, and fast-paced team combat into an experience that’s easy to jump into and rewarding to master.
As a longtime fan of the Avatar universe, this game immediately grabbed my attention. There’s something incredibly satisfying about watching beloved characters leap from the screen into a fighting game that feels so true to the world they come from. From the first match, I found myself grinning at familiar abilities, character interactions, and bending styles brought to life in exciting new ways.
What impressed me most is how distinct every fighter feels. Experimenting with different team combinations kept me coming back for “just one more match” as I discovered new strategies and synergies. Fans of games like Dragon Ball FighterZ , Marvel vs. Capcom , and Power Rangers: Battle for the Grid will recognize the thrill of building a team and learning how each character complements the others.
There’s plenty to learn with its tag mechanics and assists, but the journey of improving feels rewarding and keeps every victory exciting. Whether you grew up with “Avatar: The Last Airbender,” fell in love with “The Legend of Korra,” or simply enjoy energetic team-based fighting games, Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game captures the heart of the franchise while delivering a fun and action-packed experience that’s hard to put down.
From the moment I started playing Mewgenics , I knew I was in for a wild ride. From Edmund McMillen, the developer behind The Binding of Isaac , Super Meat Boy , and The End is Nigh , Mewgenics is a roguelike tactical turn-based RPG presented in a unique and cartoonish macabre art style, filled with dark humor and clever references.
Mewgenics offers a staggering amount of content that easily demands over a hundred hours of playtime, complete with deep strategy and a generational breeding system (yes, you breed mutant cats).
The game hooks you right away with its chaotic setup, you’re managing a house full of mutated cats and sending them out on tactical, grid-based runs. Every item, skill, and attribute is randomized, meaning no two runs ever play out the same way. When your cats survive a brutal dungeon crawl, they bring back scars and mutations that you can pass down to future generations. Breeding the ultimate mutant cat squad and trying to balance their weird genetic traits became an obsession.
The dark and sometimes graphic humor and the relentless difficulty might not be for everyone, but for me, it hit the right buttons. Mewgenics easily eats dozens of hours, keeping you hooked on trying just one more run. Mewgenics creates something entirely fresh, endlessly repayable, and wonderfully grotesque, fur-real!.
The Sinking City 2 takes the series in a bold new direction, delivering a third-person Lovecraftian survival horror experience set in a flooded 1929 Arkham. The story follows Calvin Rafferty as he searches for a way to save his fiancée, Faye, who has been trapped in a supernatural slumber after a ritual gone wrong.
From the moment I stepped into Arkham’s flooded streets armed with little more than a flashlight and a pistol, the game nailed its horror atmosphere. Traveling between districts by boat gives the city an open feel, while interconnected environments, puzzle-solving, investigation mechanics, and scarce resources keep the tension high.
What truly sets The Sinking City 2 apart, however, is its enemy design. Familiar Lovecraftian creatures provide plenty of frantic encounters, but the real stars are the Slither: parasitic worms that survive after their host dies. If ignored, they can crawl into nearby corpses, reanimate them, and force you to fight the same enemies all over again. This simple but brilliant mechanic transformed every multi-enemy encounter into a desperate scramble and created a constant sense of dread.
I don’t think I sat down once while playing The Sinking City 2 . Between its unsettling atmosphere, intriguing mystery, satisfying survival horror gameplay, and genuinely frightening enemies, it stands out as one of the genre’s most memorable experiences and a must-play for horror fans.
Woodo is that takes the cozy puzzle genre and turns it into something closer to a child’s toy box coming to life as it tells you a story. The puzzles put you in the position of assembling handcrafted wooden dioramas piece by piece, watching each empty, colorless scene slowly fill with detail, animation, and life as you click objects into their correct spots. It’s a small, tactile premise, but it’s executed with a level of care that makes every placement feel extraordinarily satisfying.
The narrative at the heart of Woodo is a story about Foxy, a city girl sent to the countryside for the summer, and her growing friendship with a local villager, who happens to be a frog named, well, Ben the Frog. The narrative unfolds across a series of interconnected dioramas, each one capturing a different moment from their shared adventure, guided by a warm, friendly narrator’s voice that makes the whole experience feel less like a puzzle game and more like a warm, cuddly bedtime story. And while the gameplay is generally pretty simple, there is some complexity to it. The assembly of the wood

articles.title_orig: Astronaut Christina Koch’s Eagles weekend was out of this world
articles.title_zh: Astronaut Christina Koch’s Eagles weekend was out of this world
articles.content_orig:
It's no secret that Eagles fans are a dedicated fanbase. However, only one can say that they have watched the team from space.
The Eagles celebrated Astronaut Christina Koch at Lincoln Financial Field as the Eagles' Honorary Captain during Sunday's game against the Rams. Known for circumnavigating the moon earlier this year with the Artemis II mission and crew, Koch also holds the world record for the longest time spent on the International Space Station in one deployment, with 328 straight days.
Even while orbiting 250 miles above the Earth's surface on the International Space Station, Koch would tune in for Eagles games.
"We have the ability to have an internet connection for personal things, crew choice things they call it. It's just a way to have things that can keep you entertained on the weekends and things that you love and remind you of home," Koch said. "I did marry into it. My husband (Robert) is a diehard, long-term Eagles fan since he was a kid. I resisted a little while mainly because I didn't know a lot about football ... now I'm all in and I've been sort of addicted ever since.
"If I didn't have time to watch them because they were at a different time where I couldn't make it, I would watch the reruns on the NFL Network or something like that. And it was just such a treat when I could share that with my husband and other people on Earth. It was a way of connecting through that and to just kick back and have a little bit of fun."
Astronaut (and Eagles fan) Christina Koch received a hero's welcome as an Honorary Captain against the Rams. After Sunday's game, the Artemis II crew member spent time with Eagles rookies, as well as science students from the Franklin Institute on Monday.

While Koch had been to Eagles games in-person before, she had never been to a home game at Lincoln Financial Field until Sunday. Not only did she join the Eagles Captains for the coin toss, Koch also led nearly 70,000 fans in an E-A-G-L-E-S chant during the two-minute warning of the first half. The woman who â quite literally â had ventured out into where no human has been before, said she was scared to start the Eagles' fight song.
"It was amazing to be at this place I've heard so much about, a place I looked at from space where I knew that all these fans came together with how dedicated they are," Koch said. "Just to be surrounded by that energy, to be right next to the players on the field, to watch their focus, watch them practice, watch their preparation rituals, it was amazing. I'm completely honored to have that opportunity."
Of course, Koch herself is no stranger to performing under pressure. During her time at the International Space Station, she participated in the first-ever all-female spacewalk, watching continents fly by below her feet as the station traveled at 17,500 miles an hour. For the Artemis II mission, Koch and the other astronauts trained for nearly three years, preparing for every single scenario â everything that could go wrong.
Koch's visit to the Eagles organization was part of NASA's Inspiration Tour, following the success of the Artemis II mission where Koch and the rest of the crew orbited farther from earth than any humans before. As it turns out, one of the many inspired by Artemis II was an Eagles Cheerleader. Before Sunday's game, Megan McKeon, a second-year cheerleader, had the opportunity to tell Koch that the mission inspired her to pursue a master's degree in planetary sciences.
"That moment was probably one of the most memorable and amazing ones of the whole game because she took the time to share her story personally with me and I could tell how much it meant to her and it truly did make an actual difference in her life," Koch said.
"I've been hearing stories like that from a lot of different people, but to meet someone firsthand that could tell me that they took the inspiration that the mission gave them and did something with it was really amazing. That was really all we ever wanted as a crew, was for it to have a positive impact on people's lives."
Koch also met Saquon Barkley on Saturday while touring the Jefferson Health Training Complex. The All-Pro running back had heard Koch was in the Eagles facility and set out to find her.
"He was super into space and the mission," Koch said.
The day after the game, the record-breaking astronaut spent time with Eagles rookies, as well as science students from the Franklin Institute on Monday. After being part of the Eagles' gameday experience, Koch got to show the Eagles rookies a glimpse into her world, answering questions before exploring the exhibits at the institute.
"Truth be told, that team inspires me, how they come into the arena and do their jobs under all that enormous, enormous pressure," Koch said. "It's been a source of inspiration. So, to be able to see it firsthand was really special." - Written by Caroline Connor

articles.title_zh: EVERY MEDALLIST AT THE WORLD CLIMBING EUROPE YOUTH SERIES LEIPZIG 2026
articles.content_orig:
Austria, Poland and France shared the four Speed gold medals as the 2026 European youth season concluded in Germany
The 2026 World Climbing Europe Youth Series concluded in Leipzig, Germany, on 3 October, with Speed medals awarded in the Under 17 and Under 19 age categories.
Austria, Poland and France shared the four gold medals, while the host nation collected three medals in total: one silver and two bronze.
UNDER 17 GOLDS FOR HASELWANTER AND MYŚLIWIEC
Austria’s Lara Haselwanter won the women’s Under 17 title in 7.30 seconds in the gold-medal race, as Slovenia’s Zoja Leskovar fell and took silver. Germany’s Lea Voigt secured bronze on home soil, clocking 9.08 against Italy’s Carolina Mariani, who also slipped and did not complete her race.
The men’s Under 17 gold-medal race was an all-Polish contest, with Maksymilian Myśliwiec taking gold in 5.83 seconds after Antoni Marcisz fell. Germany’s Maximilian Ruhland completed the podium, winning the bronze-medal race in 8.48 ahead of compatriot Moritz Müller, who clocked 9.42.
FRANCE SECURES DOUBLE GOLD IN UNDER 19 EVENTS
Eva-Lina Rymasz claimed women’s Under 19 gold for France, winning in 7.88 seconds ahead of Italy’s Alice Marcelli, who finished in 8.47. Ukraine’s Mariia Shymkova took bronze in 8.44 after Germany’s Mina Josephine Schultz slipped and fell in the bronze-medal race.
France’s Léo Grosset added men’s Under 19 gold to his country’s medal tally. Grosset clocked 5.23 in the final against Germany’s Mika Scherer, who fell but took silver. Switzerland’s Gilles Meili won bronze in 4.93 against fellow Swiss climber Sofiane Vial, who was unable to complete the race.
Following the release of next year's international competition calendar, the 2027 European events calendar will also be presented in the coming days.
All European events have been live streamed on the World Climbing Europe YouTube channel and are available on demand. News and updates about all World Climbing events will be available on the World Climbing website , and on the Federation’s digital channels: Facebook , Instagram , LinkedIn , Threads , TikTok , X , YouTube , and exclusively for the Chinese audience, Douyin, Weibo , and Xiaohongshu.

articles.title_orig: Cornell students hold sit-in over alleged 2024 fraternity assault
articles.title_zh: Cornell students hold sit-in over alleged 2024 fraternity assault
articles.content_orig:
ITHACA, N.Y. — Cornell University students began a seven-hour sit-in Wednesday in solidarity with Jane Doe, the woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted by members of the Chi Phi fraternity nearly two years ago.
“Seven hours for the seven hours she endured. Seven hours of solidarity. Seven hours demanding change,” a coalition of Cornell student groups said in a post on Instagram ahead of the demonstration.
Roughly 80 students had gathered inside a campus dining hall named for Pulitzer Prize-winning author Toni Morrison by around 3 p.m. The organizers said the sit-in is part of “Zero Day,” an “economic blackout calling on students to disrupt business as usual by not attending class or spending on campus.”
The protest illustrates the tense mood on the Ivy League campus following Jane Doe’s allegations that she was sexually assaulted and plied with drugs Oct. 19-20, 2024. She filed a civil lawsuit against the university and seven fraternity members last month, leading to renewed national attention on sexual misconduct and collegiate Greek life.
Three of the accused men have publicly denied the allegations through attorneys.
The sit-in comes two days after Cornell faculty members introduced a resolution calling for a no-confidence vote in the university administration over its handling of the alleged assault at the Chi Phi fraternity house. The resolution was submitted to the University Faculty Committee on Monday night, according to a copy obtained by NBC News.
Cornell has drawn intense scrutiny over how it responded to Jane Doe’s allegations in November 2024, and Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten has been criticized for declining to charge the accused. The university and the district attorney have each defended their original 2024 probes.
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul effectively replaced Van Houten as lead investigator last week, appointing state Attorney General Letitia James to oversee the case. Cornell and Van Houten have publicly welcomed James’ involvement. “I trust that she will examine the facts and apply the law,” Van Houten said in a statement on Friday.
Wednesday’s sit-in was announced on Instagram by a group of campus organizations, including Black Students United, Cornell NAACP, Mecha de Cornell, Planned Parenthood Generation Action at Cornell, Students for a Democratic Cornell, and a student-run chapter of the American Civil Liberties Union.
“The sit-in will be a space for students to share their support for survivors of sexual violence in myriad ways, including the share of resources and teach-ins,” the student groups said on Instagram.
Daniel Arkin is a senior reporter at NBC News.
Adam Reiss is a reporter and producer for NBC and MSNBC.

articles.title_orig: World Commemorates October 7 Ahead of Christian Summit
articles.title_zh: World Commemorates October 7 Ahead of Christian Summit
articles.content_orig:
Stand for Israel | October 7, 2026
Three years ago today, Israel and her people endured the most horrific acts of terror in the nation’s modern history on October 7, 2023. The Holy Land held its National Day of Remembrance earlier this week, but Jews and Christians in the U.S. and around the world are taking today to remember the more than 1,200 victims, the 251 people who were kidnapped, and the countless lives and communities that continue to be affected.
JNS reports that Israel’s envoy to the Christian world George Deek praised the Flags of Fellowship movement ahead of the annual Friends of Zion Ambassador Summit.
Three years after October 7, to see millions of Christians around the world publicly raise Israel’s flag is a powerful reminder that friendship can speak louder than hatred. More than 5.2 million Israeli flags, over 4,375 churches, universities and organizations, in 14 countries. WOW.
At a time when Israel and the Jewish people have faced extraordinary hatred, millions of Christians are choosing something different: friendship, remembrance and solidarity. I am deeply grateful to the International Fellowship of Christians and Jews, to Yael Eckstein, and to every pastor, church and community taking part in this remarkable initiative.
To our Christian friends around the world: thank you for standing with Israel. We see you. We appreciate you. And we will never take your friendship for granted.
The Friends of Zion Ambassador Summit will run through October 11, coinciding with Flags of Fellowship. More than 1,000 Christian leaders and influencers from 117 countries arrived in Israel on Monday for the second consecutive year of the summit. Around 300 of the participants are between the ages of 18 and 29. Summit founder Mike Evans says he hopes young Christians will see Israel for themselves and hear directly from those affected by October 7.
Much like Flags of Fellowship, the Friends of Zion Ambassador Summit carries the powerful message that Israel does not stand alone, building connections based on truth, courage, and a determination to confront anti-Semitism.
The Fellowship and our supporters pray for the families and remember the victims of October 7 alongside the 4,375 churches and synagogues around the world participating in Flags of Fellowship and the Christian ambassadors who have just arrived in Israel.

articles.title_orig: Rising seas threaten the world’s migratory shorebirds
articles.title_zh: Rising seas threaten the world’s migratory shorebirds
articles.content_orig:
Birds undertake some of the world’s most impressive migrations , travelling hundreds to thousands of kilometres every year in search of safe breeding grounds and seasonally abundant food resources. For many birds, migration is the key to their success . However, migration can also make species more vulnerable to threats.
Shorebirds — species that include sandpipers, plovers and oystercatchers — live and migrate along the world’s coastlines. Over the last several decades, coastal development has led to the loss of shorebird habitats in many areas of the world, driving population declines in multiple species . Now, a new threat is emerging: climate change-driven sea-level rise.
But how exactly does sea-level rise impact shorebirds, and just how serious is this threat?
Our new study reviews the evidence from 37 published papers to provide the first comprehensive overview of the threat of sea-level rise to the world’s shorebirds. Long story short: things aren’t looking good.
Shorebirds — as their name suggests — live along the shore, relying primarily on coastal ecosystems like  beaches, salt marshes and tidal flats. As sea levels rise, these vital habitats shrink.
Some coastal ecosystems may persist in the face of sea-level rise by moving inland with the rising waters, but this isn’t always possible. More than half of the world’s largest cities are within 100 kilometres of a coast , meaning that the presence of coastal infrastructure often blocks these pathways.
This leads to a phenomenon known as coastal squeeze — where ecosystems are increasingly squeezed between the rising waters and an inland barrier (such as dikes and seawalls built to protect homes and businesses), leading to decreases in habitat.
Loss of habitat has obvious implications for migratory shorebirds: less access to food, less space for nesting and more competition with other individuals.
But habitat loss isn’t the only threat to these species. Sea-level rise may also impact shorebirds in different ways, leading to changes in prey distribution , reproductive success , feeding time and many other factors.
Among the 37 studies that we examined, 21 predicted negative impacts of sea-level rise on shorebird habitats such as declines in habitat area or quality, while 17 predicted negative impacts on shorebird populations or individuals such as decreased survival or abundance.
Sea-level rise is expected to drive substantial habitat loss at many sites of international importance for migratory shorebirds. These include San Francisco Bay and Humboldt Bay in the United States, the Colorado River Delta and Marismas Nacionales in Mexico and the Yellow Sea region in East Asia, each of which supports 150,000 to more than one million shorebirds annually.
Habitat loss at these kinds of migratory bottleneck sites where large numbers of shorebirds congregate over a short period of time may hit populations particularly hard. Because so many birds funnel through these sites during migration, habitat loss in these areas may impact multiple species and entire populations. This means these sites must be a priority for conservation.
Maintaining coastal ecosystems and protecting them from the threat of sea-level rise will be essential for the survival of thriving shorebird populations. But coastal ecosystems aren’t only important for shorebirds. They also support thousands of other species and provide valuable ecosystem services such as coastal protection, water filtration and carbon storage.
In order to preserve these habitats and the species that depend on them, governments will need to make a serious effort to mitigate the impacts of coastal squeeze. Rather than continuing to armour our shorelines, decision makers should prioritize solutions that will protect human communities while also benefitting coastal ecosystems .
The shape that these actions take may vary from place to place. In some areas, it may be necessary to relocate coastal infrastructure to give ecosystems space to move inland as sea levels rise — an approach referred to as “managed retreat.” In other areas, scientists and practitioners are looking at how we can use sediment recovered from dredging to enhance or create new habitats.
However we choose to respond to sea-level rise, urgent action will be required to preserve shorebirds and their fascinating migrations for generations to come.

articles.title_orig: AEW Grand Slam: France Dynamite Results – Will Ospreay Keeps AEW World Title from Okada, Mercedes Moné Retains AEW Women’s World Title vs. Queen Aminata, More
articles.title_zh: AEW Grand Slam: France Dynamite Results – Will Ospreay Keeps AEW World Title from Okada, Mercedes Moné Retains AEW Women’s World Title vs. Queen Aminata, More
articles.content_orig:
AEW's debut in Paris was a special one, as Grand Slam: France Dynamite emanated from Adidas Arena on TBS and HBO Max! A major debut called for a huge card, and Paris responded with energy that could be felt from the opening bell and beyond the main event! As if the excitement wasn’t high enough, we’re just 11 days from AEW WrestleDream in Orlando!
In the main event, AEW World Champion Will Ospreay defeated AEW International Champion “The Rainmaker” Kazuchika Okada to retain his title in an unbelievable match, which marked the first time Ospreay beat Okada in a championship bout. As Ospreay celebrated in the ring with “Speedball” Mike Bailey, Samoa Joe appeared on the ramp to end the night, sending a message that he’s ready for Clockwork Carnage after qualifying by beating “Jungle” Jack Perry earlier in the night.
AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné got everything she could handle from Queen Aminata in front of a Parisian crowd that was fully behind Aminata’s quest to win her first AEW gold. Moné overcame Aminata in the end to get the win, but she could not celebrate for long because her WrestleDream opponent, Thekla, hit the ring to cut Moné in half with a spear!
The night began with ROH World Champion Bandido turning away AEW World Trios Champion Kofi while both men’s trios partners made their presence felt, specifically Swerve Strickland and “Hangman” Adam Page. Later, Swerve and The New Level challenged Page, Bandido and Brody King to face them in a 2-out-of-3 falls match for the AEW World Trios Championship at WrestleDream!
TNT Champion Darby Allin was left a bloody mess in his defense against former champion “The Protostar” Kyle Fletcher, but somehow Allin was able to leave Paris with a successful defense in a brutally violent encounter.  Plus, Mark Davis and Jake Doyle earned a huge win for the Don Callis Family in tag team action over Gabe Kidd and AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley!
All that and more went down on our first night in Paris!
The night began with the ROH World Championship on the line! Kofi, one third of the AEW World Trios Champions, made his way to the ring to a raucous ovation inside the Adidas Arena, accompanied by another third of the champions, Austin Creed.
The champion came out next, and he wasn't alone either — Bandido was flanked by Brody King for this championship tilt.
The referee called for the Code of Honor, and not only did both men shake hands, but they embraced. A hyped-up crowd was fully behind this matchup, which only fed the energy of both Kofi and Bandido.
While both men brought a clear level of speed, there was an extended feeling-out process to start, with each grabbing a brief advantage before the action reset to a stalemate. After both went for dropkicks, Bandido popped right back to his feet, but Kofi came back with a second dropkick that sent Bandido to the floor. When Kofi tried to dive to the outside, Bandido simply stepped out of the way, and Kofi's head bounced off the top rope. Bandido tried to climb back to the apron, but Kofi caught him with another dropkick, knocking him to the floor again. Kofi then charged and flipped over the top rope onto the floor, crushing Bandido, and took control of the early going.
Kofi rolled Bandido back into the ring and climbed the ropes. As Bandido got to his feet, Kofi leaped off the top for a cross body — but Bandido caught him in mid-air and, in an incredible display of strength, lifted him into a delayed vertical suplex, holding him aloft one-armed as the crowd counted all the way to twenty before finally dropping him to the mat.
The sheer exhaustion of that suplex left both men down. It was then that Swerve Strickland, the third member of the AEW World Trios Champions, made his way out with Prince Nana to join Creed in supporting Kofi. Only steps behind him, however, was “Hangman” Adam Page, and when Swerve spotted him, Creed and Nana had to hold him back. Page simply walked past and joined King at ringside to support their partner.
Bandido played to the crowd before turning his attention back to Kofi, landing a pair of corner strikes followed by a diving gut check that doubled Kofi over in pain. Bandido fired off more strikes in an adjacent corner, but when he went for a third, Kofi slipped away and whipped him to the opposite corner. With Bandido seated against the turnbuckle, Kofi drove a running knee into the side of his face, followed by elevated stomps to the chest. Kofi then ran in from the opposite corner for a shotgun dropkick, connecting flush. He covered, but Bandido kicked out to keep his title reign alive.
A visibly frustrated Kofi took a moment to regroup before pulling Bandido up, hitting a headbutt and an uppercut to back him into the corner and hoist him up top for a superplex attempt. But when Kofi came up after him, Bandido turned it around with a gorilla press slam, dumping Kofi onto the top turnbuckle before following with a dropkick that put him on the mat! Bandido covered, but Kofi kicked out at two.
Bandido tried to whip Kofi across the ring, but Kofi reversed it with a kick to the stomach, then leaped for a leg drop to the back of Bandido's head. Kofi started building momentum, landing backhanded chops followed by a jumping side kick that put Bandido back down. Bandido avoided a follow-up jumping clothesline and whipped Kofi to the corner, but as he rushed in, Kofi flipped back with a pendulum kick through the ropes, then went up top for a frog splash cross body that got another near-fall.
Kofi bounced off the ropes for a jumping lariat, then fired up the Paris crowd before connecting with a Boom Drop. As Bandido stumbled to his feet, Kofi measured him for T.I.P., but Bandido ducked out of the way. Kofi spun him around in a rear waistlock and sent him to the corner. Bandido kicked his way out and leaped to the top rope for a reverse tornillo that got a two-count.
Bandido pushed Kofi into the ropes, but Kofi rebounded with a jumping spin kick to the head for another near-fall. The crowd roared as Bandido started to fight back, only for Kofi to cut him off with a kick to the gut. The two traded strikes off the ropes until Bandido popped Kofi up into a knee strike. As Bandido came off the ropes, Kofi leaped into the air and stomped him into the mat.
The crowd was fully invested as both men's partners continued to will them on from ringside. Bandido rose in the corner as Kofi waited in the opposite one; when Kofi charged in, Bandido met him with a kick combination and climbed to the second rope. As Bandido came off, Kofi caught him and rolled him through for an SOS into the second buckle! That’s a new and brutal variation on that move, matching Bandido's own escalating viciousness in this battle for championship gold.
As Creed and Swerve, along with the crowd, urged Kofi toward the top rope, he slowly made his way up. With Bandido doubled over below, Kofi leaped off and splashed him flat onto his back! That was an unorthodox execution, but even more devastating!  Bandido kicked out to preserve his reign!
Kofi dug deeper into his arsenal than ever before, fully aware of the caliber of champion standing across from him. He made his way back to the top rope, but with Creed's back turned to hype the crowd, nobody saw Bandido sneak up from behind to catch Kofi with a kick. Bandido joined him on the top rope, and with both men balanced precariously, Bandido grabbed Kofi and hit a Revolutionary Fly from the top! He covered, 1-2-Kofi got a hand on the bottom rope to stay alive! Bandido picked up Kofi for the X-Knee, but Kofi landed on his feet and hit an SOS for a near-fall!
An argument broke out between Hangman and Swerve at ringside, and the two got in a shoving match, with both men having to be separated from each other. In the ensuing commotion, Bandido pulled Kofi off the mat with the 21 Plex for the three-count. As Bandido celebrated, Page and Swerve still had to be separated, with King telling Page that all that matters is that Band

articles.title_orig: WHO endorses lifestyle changes over GLP-1 drugs in child obesity fight
articles.title_zh: WHO endorses lifestyle changes over GLP-1 drugs in child obesity fight
articles.content_orig:
The first-ever international guidelines on managing childhood obesity from the World Health Organization (WHO) are raising the profile of GLP-1 treatments for kids and teens — but with strict criteria and a high degree of caution.
The new global guidance, released on Wednesday , recommends a broad range of interventions to manage diet, boost physical activity and change behaviours for the rising number of global youth living with obesity. And in certain cases, for some older children and teenagers, that could also mean medication or bariatric surgery.
The WHO doesn't recommend medical treatment, surgery or weight-loss devices for children up to the age of nine, the organization notes.
For older youth from the age of 10 to 19, medical treatments may be considered only when a supervised lifestyle program hasn't achieved results, the guidance states, while bariatric surgery should only be an option under strict conditions for youth living with severe obesity.
"The foundation of obesity care for children and adolescents is not medicine or surgery, but access to comprehensive support that enables healthy eating, physical activity and sustainable behaviour change," said Dr. Luz María De Regil, the WHO's director of the department of nutrition and food safety.
Cheaper GLP-1s arrive in Canada: Are they safe?
London, Ont.-based pediatric endocrinologist Dr. Marina Ybarra welcomed the organization's cautious acknowledgement of medications as one avenue to tackle obesity.
Here in Canada, two GLP-1s are approved for weight management for youth aged 12 and up, but young patients typically have to pay for the drugs through their parents' insurance or out of pocket, said Ybarra, who works with Western University and leads the London Health Sciences Centre Children's Hospital pediatric weight management clinic.
Obesity Canada launches partnership aimed at improving care in health system
"The news about WHO encouraging GLP-1 as a possible treatment for children living with obesity — I think it's very good news," she said.
"Because maybe that will help us to get funding through the public system in Canada for children living with obesity. That's my biggest hope."
The WHO's new guidance is meant to tackle skyrocketing rates of obesity among global youth.
Roughly 170 million children and teens around the world between the ages of five to 19 were living with obesity in 2024, the WHO noted. Obesity prevalence in this age group has also quadrupled since 1990, rising from two to eight per cent.
The global recommendations echo recent Canadian guidance to manage obesity in children. That long-awaited 2025 update also called for behavioural and psychological support and, in some cases, additional medical or surgical interventions.
How family doctors navigate the rise of weight loss drugs
Can GLP-1s curb more than your desire for food?
But Canadian physicians recommend only using GLP-1s to manage obesity in children after the age of 12, two years above the WHO's cutoff due, and don't stipulate that medical intervention should only be tried after lifestyle changes.
" There is no evidence to support a stepwise approach whereby pharmacologic and surgical interventions should be offered only if behavioural and psychological interventions prove ineffective," reads the guidance published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal.
"Using shared decision-making with families, health care providers should consider all intervention options."
The WHO, in contrast, focused on the "practicality and universality" of diet, physical activity and behavioural changes as the pillars of obesity management, and it stressed the need for "structured long-term follow-up" in cases where patients use medication alongside other lifestyle interventions.
Weight comes back quickly after quitting GLP-1 drugs: study
GLP-1s and other similar medications — known by household brand names like Ozempic, Mounjaro, Rybelsus, Wegovy and Zepbound — have exploded in popularity among adults to treat obesity and diabetes, and for general weight loss, even without a clear medical need .
The drugs work by mimicking the body's glucagon-like peptide-1 hormone, which helps manage appetite, slow digestion and regulate blood sugar.
Ybarra stressed the medications are now an effective tool for many young patients with obesity, helping to both reduce weight and improve quality of life.
1st generic semaglutide injection for weight loss approved: Health Canada
While some children and teens face similar side effects to older patients, including nausea and other gastrointestinal issues, "we didn't see many of the severe complications that were seen in the adult population," Ybarra noted.
Younger and younger patients are also trying this growing class of drugs.
One U.S. study, published in the medical journal Pediatrics in September , revealed a 310-fold increase in GLP-1 prescriptions for children ages eight to 11, shooting up from 0.03 per cent to more than nine per cent between 2019 and 2026 — though overall use in this younger group remains rare.
Should everyone be on GLP-1s? What the science really tells us about cancer prevention and other benefits
Still, the WHO stressed the need for caution regarding GLP-1 use among children and teens, given limited research and the potential for misuse among certain groups, such as athletes or patients with eating disorders.
The WHO's new guidelines note that overall evidence linked to various medication treatments for childhood obesity, including GLP-1s and other drugs such as metformin or sibutramine, was "generally of low quality due to short term follow-up and evaluation, and [due to] the small numbers of studies and participants."
Ybarra agreed there's a lack of long-term data for the use of GLP-1s among youth, given how new these drugs are for younger patients.
"The data we have though, it's very reassuring and helpful — in terms of there's more benefits than risks."
GLP-1s and cancer prevention: What’s known and what isn’t
As for the line in the sand regarding children under 10 avoiding GLP-1s, the WHO's María De Regil stressed in a Tuesday news conference that the agency "recommends prioritizing other interventions in this age group."
"However, it is clear that the research is going in this area," she said. "Some national pediatric associations may recommend it."
Serena Williams’ return to tennis sparks conversation about GLP-1 drugs in sports
Denmark's Novo Nordisk and U.S.-based Eli Lilly are among the drug makers currently trialling pediatric obesity medications for kids as young as six, though María De Regil wouldn’t speculate on how any of those ongoing trials might change the WHO's recommendations.
Major questions still remain about how children should safely use these types of drugs, and for how long, stressed María De Regil.
"We realize that this is a rapidly evolving field," she said.
Senior Health & Medical Reporter
Lauren Pelley is a senior health and medical reporter for CBC News. She's a two-time RNAO Media Award winner for in-depth health reporting in 2020 and 2022, a silver medallist for best editorial newsletter at the 2024 Digital Publishing Awards, and a 2024 Covering Climate Now award winner in the health category. Contact her at: lauren.pelley@cbc.ca.

articles.title_orig: 2 of the best resorts in the world are in New England, according to Conde Nast Traveler readers
articles.title_zh: 2 of the best resorts in the world are in New England, according to Conde Nast Traveler readers
articles.content_orig:
Add Boston.com as your preferred source on Google to see more of our stories.
Two seaside resorts in New England are among the best on the planet, according to Conde Nast Traveler readers.
The travel publication released a list of the 50 best resorts in the world on Tuesday, part of its 39th Annual Readers’ Choice Awards , and Chatham Bars Inn in Chatham ranked No. 18. Weekapaug Inn in Westerly, R.I. ranked No. 28.
Chatham Bars Inn , which was also named the No. 1 resort in New England , is “a benchmark of luxury on the Cape,” Conde Nast Traveler wrote.
“If you’re looking for a full-service resort with all the bells and whistles and then some, this is it, including an eight-acre private farm to stock the resort’s numerous dining and drinking outlets; one of the better spas on the Cape; an expansive pool deck with F&B service; a private quarter-mile beachfront; tennis courts with lessons available; and a 24-hour gym,” wrote the publication.
Resort officials celebrated on social media , writing, “Thank you to our incredible team and to our guests and supporters who voted for us. We’re grateful to be recognized alongside so many remarkable destinations.”
Weekapaug Inn, also named the No. 2 resort in New England , is a historic getaway in Rhode Island.
“A recently renovated legendary seaside inn on the National Register of Historic Places, the 27-room, six-suite Weekapaug Inn is a three-hour drive from New York and less than two from Boston—ideal for a quick weekend jaunt,” wrote Conde Nast Traveler .
Visitors enjoy guided nature walks, golf, tennis, and boating expeditions in historic vessels, noted the publication.
Officials at Weekapaug Inn also shared their excitement on social media , writing, “Thank you to the Condé Nast Traveler readers who voted, and to our incredible teams for truly delivering the best of service, cuisine, and luxury, year after year. We hope to share our award-winning experiences with you soon.”

articles.title_orig: Honda World housing plan returns with limited revisions
articles.title_zh: Honda World housing plan returns with limited revisions
articles.content_orig:
DOWNEY – A controversial proposal to replace the former Honda World service center with townhomes returns to the Planning Commission on Wednesday with one fewer home and limited design changes following opposition from residents and the commission’s unanimous July vote to deny the project.
Meritage Homes’ revised plan calls for 144 townhomes instead of 145. It adds 22 open parking spaces, increases setbacks in two areas and lowers three homes along the southern property line from three stories to two. The remaining 141 homes would still be three stories.
The commission voted unanimously July 15 to deny the original 145-unit proposal, citing traffic and safety concerns. But when commissioners met Aug. 19 to consider a formal denial resolution, they instead agreed to reconsider the project at a future public hearing, giving the developer time to address concerns.
City planning staff again recommends approval.
The revised proposal increases open parking from 40 to 62 spaces, a gain of 22 spaces, or 55%. Each home would also have a two-car garage, bringing the development’s total parking supply to 350 spaces.
Along Fairford Avenue, the developer increased the proposed front setback from 10 feet to 15 feet.
Removing a home at the northwest corner would increase Building 1’s rear setback from 9 feet to 25.2 feet from the existing block wall. The revised distance to the property line would be 35.8 feet, according to the staff report.
Three homes along the southern property line would be reduced from three stories to two. Those homes would have enclosed ground-floor private yards instead of second-story balconies.
The developer also widened the central communal open space by 2 feet.
Most of the development would remain three stories, with a maximum proposed height of 37 feet, 6 inches. The two-, three- and four-bedroom homes would be distributed among 14 buildings. Planned community amenities include a shade structure, barbecue counter, picnic area, benches and a children’s play structure.
Vehicle access would be provided through a driveway on Dollison Drive allowing entry and exit, and an entrance-only driveway on Fairford Avenue.
At the July hearing, 24 of the 26 public speakers opposed the project. Residents raised concerns about neighborhood compatibility, privacy, parking overflow, traffic congestion and speeding. Supporters cited the need for affordable housing and opportunities for homeownership.
Commissioners’ denial motion focused on community safety and requested traffic changes, including a signal at Cecilia Street, a right-turn-only connection between Dollison Drive and Studebaker Avenue, and making Crossdale Avenue a dead end.
According to the new staff report, city staff reviewed those requests and determined the signal and street changes were not warranted by engineering criteria and observed traffic volumes.
A traffic study prepared for the original 145-unit proposal estimated approximately 926 daily vehicle trips, compared with 832 trips generated by the former Honda World service and parts facility, a net increase of about 94 trips.
The study concluded that eight nearby intersections would continue operating at acceptable levels and that the project would not create significant traffic capacity, operational or safety deficiencies. The city’s Traffic Engineering Division reviewed the analysis and agreed with its findings, according to the report.
Recommended approval conditions would require the developer to monitor traffic volumes and speeds after occupancy on Dollison Drive, Fairford Avenue, Crossdale Avenue and Cecilia Street. If the monitoring identifies project-related impacts warranting traffic calming, the developer would be required to implement appropriate measures.
The staff report also emphasizes limits on the city’s discretion under state housing laws. Staff concluded that the record does not establish the findings needed under the Housing Accountability Act to deny the project or require fewer homes.
The property was previously designated as a housing opportunity site, and its housing overlay already allows residential development. The applicant is requesting six development-standard waivers through the state’s density bonus law.
The Planning Commission meeting begins at 6:30 p.m. Wednesday in the City Council chambers.

articles.title_orig: Rubio Stresses Need for U.S. Security Work With Greece on Migration and Terrorism
articles.title_zh: Rubio Stresses Need for U.S. Security Work With Greece on Migration and Terrorism
articles.content_orig:
The Greeks of antiquity continue to hold a mystical grip on our memory. In 480 BC, a handful of Athenians refuse to flee and barricade themselves in the Acropolis. They fight an extraordinary last stand against Xerxes' invading army.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio took aim at open borders and globalism Wednesday in a sweeping speech in Athens, Greece that at times sounded more like a campaign stump speech than a foreign policy address.
"We opened our borders and outsourced our industry and allowed our militaries to wither and to decay," Rubio said against the backdrop of the sun setting on the ancient citadel in Athens.
"The word nationalism became a dirty word. And so we tore down our monuments, we condemned our own history, and in too many places we taught our children to be ashamed of the countries they would inherit," he continued. "And with every passing year, we seemed to outsource more of our sovereignty, transferring our decisions to global bureaucracies far beyond the reach of our control."
Rubio and Vice President JD Vance have both been widely discussed as potential successors to Trump in 2028, with the president himself repeatedly fueling speculation over which of the two could inherit his political mantle.
Rubio argued the consequences were now playing out in an increasingly dangerous world.
TRUMP’S COUNTERTERRORISM STRATEGY SCORES BIG WINS AGAINST GLOBAL TERROR THREATS
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks at the Pnyx hill, where ancient Athenians held democratic assemblies, with the ancient Parthenon temple atop the Acropolis seen in the background, in Athens,on October 7, 2026. (Mark Schiefelbein / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)
"As the West's confidence faltered, its adversaries and rivals only grew more assertive," he said.
Rubio called the current moment an "inflection point," warning that the threats facing the West are "every bit as real as they were during antiquity."
"And now there is war again. There is competition between great powers again," he said.
Rubio singled out Iran as he drew a sharp distinction between Western values and those of its adversaries.
"Fanatics like the radical mullahs of Iran, whose cult of death hails child suicide bombers as national heroes and portrays martyrdom as an end to itself," Rubio said.
"Our heroes may be willing to die for their cause, but our heroes do not worship death," he went on. "It is precisely because we value life, that we come to recognize the heroism in those who would sooner sacrifice it than to betray their principles."
The secretary of State delivered the address from the Acropolis, using the birthplace of Western civilization to trace America's own inheritance from Ancient Greece.
"For twenty-five centuries since, the Parthenon has stood. Empires have risen and fallen beneath its shadow," Rubio said.
"Two and a half centuries after the founding of the American republic halfway across the world from where I stand now, I stand here today – as the Secretary of State of that republic, and as the great-grandson of settlers who arrived in the new world from Spain – I stand here to testify to a debt that no lapse of time, no distance of space, can ever extinguish."
Secretary of State Marco Rubio meets with Greek Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis on Oct. 7, 2026, in Athens, Greece. (Milos Bicanski/Getty Images)
Rubio said he saw signs that Europe was beginning to reverse the trends he described.
"We believe that Europe can awaken from its long slumber and rekindle the fire that was lit here millennia ago," Rubio said. "There are already signs. Across this continent, we are witnessing the beginning of what we hope will be a generational shift."
During his visit, Rubio announced a new counterterrorism partnership between the U.S. and Greece.
He emphasized the strategic importance of Greece on Wednesday, calling it a "source of stability in an unstable world."
"As you see a world that faces these destabilizing events, you recognize how important this alliance with Greece is to the United States," Rubio said. "It is a source of stability in an unstable world."
At the Munich Security Conference in Germany in February, Rubio delivered a speech on the topic that earned him a standing ovation from European leaders, and racked up millions of views online. One popular X user described it as "one of the greatest" speeches by a Secretary of State in decades.
Many others insisted the speech upped Rubio's potential 2028 presidential chances.
AS AMERICA MARKS 250 YEARS, OUR GREATEST CHAPTERS ARE STILL AHEAD OF US
Rubio described the five centuries before the end of World War II, a time when the West had expanded across the globe, building "vast empires." But, he said, after the war, Europe was in ruins, and "godless communist revolutions" in Europe caused people to believe that the West's dominance was forever finished.
"Against that backdrop, then, as now, many came to believe that the West's age of dominance had come to an end, and that our future was destined to be a faint and feeble echo of our past. But together, our predecessors recognized that decline was a choice, and it was a choice they refused to make," he said.
Rubio urged the European leaders to reinvigorate that spirit.
"This is why we do not want out allies to be shackled by guilt and shame," he continued. "We want allies that are proud of our culture and our heritage, and understand that we are heirs to the same great and noble civilization and who together with us, are willing and able to defend it."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"And this is why we don't want allies to rationalize the broken status quo, rather than what is necessary to reckon with what is necessary to fix it. For we in America have no interest in being polite and orderly caretakers of the West's managed decline. We do not seek to separate, but to revitalize an old friendship and renew the greatest civilization in human history."

articles.title_orig: Tishman Speyer Takes Over Chrysler Building With Big Renovation Plans
articles.title_zh: Tishman Speyer Takes Over Chrysler Building With Big Renovation Plans
articles.content_orig:
© 2026 Observer Media · Terms · Privacy
Tishman Speyer is taking over stewardship of the landmarked Chrysler Building with plans to renovate it after signing a lengthy ground lease.
The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art , the private college which owns the land underneath the tower, finalized a deal with the commercial real estate giant that is due to last 150 years. The New York Times confirmed the ground lease Tuesday night .
The terms of the ground lease such as the monthly payments were not disclosed, but Tishman Speyer agreed to invest $235 million in upgrades in addition to ground lease payments.
Cooper Union has owned the land since 1901, and evicted Aby Rosen and Michael Fuchs ’s RFR Holding in November 2024 after a default on $21 million in ground-rent payments.
“We are pursuing an ambitious plan for the Chrysler Building at a historically strong moment for the Manhattan office market,” Tishman Speyer CEO Rob Speyer said in a statement. “Just as we have done through new developments like The Spiral and our continuous reinvention of Rockefeller Center , we will create an environment that will make our customers proud and excited to work here every day.”
Cooper Union was represented by Steve Klein , Gibson Dunn and David Heller of Savills .
“The vacancy rate is pretty significant,” Heller told Commercial Observer. “I think part of it was that there was a market dynamic in 2020, 2021, and then through the negotiations with the previous leaseholder for a new long-term, restructured ground lease. Until that was resolved, there wasn’t necessarily the motivation or incentive to continue to invest and to proactively lease up the building while those conversations were happening.”
Between RFR’s eviction and closing the deal with Tishman Speyer, Cooper Union was making the best of the opportunity to find a leaseholder who would manage the building in a way that was in the best financial interest of the school.
The repositioning plans include turning 75 percent of the building’s currently and soon-to-be vacant space into pre-built office suites in order to streamline the flow of new leases in the 77-story tower, with Tishman Speyer echoing the approach it took with 6 Grand Central .
Reports were circulating earlier in 2026 that Tishman Speyer was in talks to acquire the building, but Speyer was tight-lipped about the deal.
The new ground lease grants Cooper Union, a private college, the ability to restore full-tuition scholarships to all of its undergraduate students in line with its mission.
“For more than a century, the Chrysler Building has helped sustain Peter Cooper’s vision of opening access to education by removing financial barriers,” Steven McLaughlin , president of Cooper Union, said in a statement. “We have a responsibility to be caretakers of that promise, to build upon it, and to leave Cooper stronger for those who come after us. This agreement is part of an integrated financial plan that gives us the framework to confidently pursue that goal.”
Canada’s Public Sector Pension Investment Board is also an investor in the repositioning effort, backing Tishman Speyer.
